checkpoint10000.reason: The Orbax temporary checkpoint contains no serialized params or train_state payload and is not visible as a completed manager step. It cannot represent the optimizer/model state after 10001 updates.

failure_localization.lower_bound: The durable progress receipt for label 10000 was written after optimizer update 10001 completed.
failure_localization.upper_bound: The checkpoint save did not reach a completed Orbax step and the Python process disappeared before its finally/result receipt ran.

source_level_checkpoint_hazard.risk: The checkpoint writer may still serialize the current state while the next iteration starts and donates/reuses that state. This creates an avoidable checkpoint-lifetime and memory-overlap hazard. It is a source-level engineering hazard, but the present evidence does not prove it was the sole cause of the hard exit.

filesystem_observation.interpretation: The /data target was not space-exhausted. The nearly-full root filesystem is an infrastructure risk, but no ENOSPC evidence ties it causally to this hard exit, so it is not declared the root cause.

next_gate.name: STEP0_CHECKPOINT_SAVE_RESOURCE_AND_LIFETIME_QUALIFICATION
next_gate.purpose: Test checkpoint serialization independently of scientific training on a clean A100 host using a fresh step-0 state and no BEHAVIOR data or policy outcome access.
next_gate.stage_a: Save a fresh step-0 state under the same 40 GiB host cgroup ceiling and wait synchronously for Orbax completion.
next_gate.stage_b: Only if stage A passes, separately test the unsafe async-overlap pattern with a synthetic batch16 step to determine whether overlap/donation creates an additional failure. Stage B is diagnostic only and cannot authorize formal training by itself.
